results.notes: Required fix 1 applied in apps/Model Plane/rust/services/inference-core/src/provider/fallback.rs. attach_role was `let decision = decision?;`, which returned None for every non-role call and so dropped the budget RouteNote that resolve_intent produces when INFERENCE_ROUTE_NOTE is on (route_note_enabled().then(...) at about line 1280). It is now `match decision { None => note, Some(decision) => Some(RouteNote { role: Some(decision), ..note.unwrap_or_else(RouteNote::unbudgeted) }) }`. A non-role call keeps its note unchanged. A role call still always carries a note, unbudgeted when none exists. With the switch off, attach_role(None, None) is None, as before. The existing doc comment already described this behaviour, so it was not edited. New unit test plain_call_keeps_its_budget_note_and_a_role_call_adds_its_decision in mod resolution_tests asserts attach_role(Some(budget), None) == Some(budget), attach_role(None, None) == None, and both role-call branches. No other file changed this round, and the files_changed list is the full slice list from the previous report. The test has not run, so the fix is verified by reading only. Apply Entry A, a blank line, the separator '---', a blank line, Entry B, a blank line, '---', a blank line, Entry C, a blank line, '---', and a blank line, so the existing heading keeps its rhythm. Entry A: ## 2026-11-03 - Run now is a manual schedule fire through the same Control fire authorisation; creator only (EP-6 S2) ... Status line: **Status: decided at the default; not built yet (EP-6 S2 builds it, dark).** Decided: OD-1 (creator only), OD-8 (manual fires count toward the three-failure auto-pause) and OD-9 (limits). A creator presses Run now on one of their own schedules. The fire takes the same Control decisions as a cron fire: `AuthorizeFire` on the route, as the sweeper makes it for a cron slot, and then the task dispatcher's checks (`AuthorizeFire`, then `AuthorizeScheduledRun`) before `StartWorkflow`. Run now never calls `StartWorkflow` directly, and it writes the same `tasks` and `cron_fires` rows as a cron fire, with fire key `manual:<uuid>`. Creator only is enforced in capability-core and in the BFF. Org admins and owners keep pause and delete but cannot press Run now, because a press spends the creator's stored authority at a moment the creator did not choose. One manual fire may be in flight per schedule, and at most six manual fires per schedule per rolling hour; the refusals are typed 409 and 429. ZDR refuses the route at the capability-core router, as it refuses every non-read request from a ZDR principal. Supersedes nothing. Entry B: ## 2026-11-03 - The Automations hub shows Active, Paused and Expired; the Fleet console stays hidden until Quarry has a fleet model (EP-6 S0, OD-2, OD-3). Status line: **Status: decided at the defaults. The Fleet route is already hidden: it mounts only when `VITE_FLEET_CONSOLE` is `'1'`, and no tracked config sets it.** Decided: OD-3, the hub states are Active, Paused and Expired. Expired means the approval lapsed. Paused shows its reason (set by the owner, or after failures). There is no Completed state until one-shot schedules exist, and those are out of scope. OD-2: no producer starts a fleet, and proxying `/v1/fleets/:id` through a Quarry-audience BFF would add a cross-plane route with nothing behind it, so the console stays hidden. When Quarry rules that it has no fleet model, the code is removed rather than proxied, and EP-6 S5 removes any link to it. Supersedes nothing. Entry C: ## 2026-11-03 - Agent definitions stay in Convex and are versioned there; capability-core keeps policy only (EP-6, OD-4, OD-5, DEC-14). Status line: **Status: proposed until the owner rules on OD-4 and OD-5.** It blocks EP-6 S7 to S11; S0 to S6 do not depend on it. OD-4 (recommended: immutable published versions): each definition has numbered, immutable versions in Convex with a canonical digest, one editable draft, and a `publishedVersion` pointer on the agent. A binding or a run pins a version, and publishing never changes a running turn. Rollback publishes an old version again as a new number. OD-5 (recommended: the Convex definition holds the join): the tool allowlist and the autonomy cap live on the definition and apply tighten-only at invoke. They narrow what the WS05 bindings and the org policy already allow and never grant. capability-core stays the policy of record under DEC-14 and gains no agent table; the agent cap is one more input to the WS25-S6 strictest-wins resolve. OD-6 (named-agent authority, phase 3) is open in the depth register. Supersedes nothing.
